To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CHC22 and VAMP2, two regulators of GLUT4 transport, are upregulated during human skeletal muscle regeneration; (2) CHC22-excess mice show a delay in muscle regeneration, and (3) CHC22 is a marker for muscle regeneration.
the CHC22-GLUT4 pathway plays a role in regeneration and maintenance of fiber type in skeletal muscle.
the CHC22 clathrin isoforms contributes to skeletal muscle regeneration in mice and humans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel role for the GLUT4 pathway during muscle regeneration.
the role of the GLUT4 transport pathway in skeletal muscle.
the molecular mechanisms that control the trafficking of the GLUT4 vesicle in skeletal muscle and how defects in these processes contribute to the development of type 2 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GLUT4 transport pathway is required for normal regeneration of skeletal muscle in mice and humans.
the GLUT4 pathway plays an important role in skeletal muscle regeneration in both mice and humans.
the GLUT4-CHC22-VAMP2 pathway plays a critical role in the regeneration of skeletal muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GLUT4 pathway contributes to muscle regeneration and that CHC22 and VAMP2 are potential biomarkers for muscle regeneration.
the CHC22-GLUT4 transport pathway plays a role in skeletal muscle regeneration in mice and humans.
we show that a clathrin isoforms, CHC22, that is expressed in a limited number of tissues and species is involved in a specialized pathway for GLUT4 glucose transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CHC22 and its associated proteins are markers of muscle regeneration.
the CHC22/ GLUT4 pathway plays a role in muscle repair.
GLUT4 transport is important for muscle regeneration.
